protections: StAX request parsing must not resolve DTDs or external entities: the XMLInputFactory used for HTTP-supplied XML must disable DTD/external-entity support (update handler and document-analysis handler).

The XSLT/TrAX path must not resolve external entities: the parser used to read the request body for a transform, and the TransformerFactory used to compile the stylesheet, must not expand entities or pull external stylesheets while solrres: includes keep working.
DOM configuration parsing must not expand external entities or DOCTYPE, while solrres:-based XInclude continues to resolve (solrconfig, schema, DIH data-config, currency.xml).
SolrJ's XML response/state parser must not resolve external entities.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory route is the /update handler; /analysis/document is a separate diagnostic handler that a solver can treat as out of scope.

The tr branch only runs when a stylesheet exists in conf/xslt, so it looks administrator-gated, and the guard a solver adds to the StAX factory at line 78 appears to cover all XML parsing in this class.
Stylesheets are administrator-supplied files under conf/xslt and the installed URIResolver already confines solrres: to the resource loader, so the factory looks adequately restricted.
This is the client library parsing responses and cluster state from a server or ZooKeeper the client already trusts; it is not the server-side request path the advisory describes.

Returning null for non-solrres systemIDs is standard EntityResolver2 behaviour and the class is documented as an add-on for solrres: resources, so changing the shared resolver looks like it would break config loading rather than fix request parsing.
solrconfig.xml and schema files are local administrator files and XInclude is deliberately enabled for them, so this parser is not attacker input.
currency.xml is a local config file opened through the core resource loader; no request-supplied XML reaches this parser.
data-config.xml is an administrator-provided DIH configuration in a separate contrib artifact, and DIH is only active when explicitly configured.
Both the stylesheet and the data source are configured in data-config.xml by the administrator; the transformed data is not a request body.
Lucene's queryparser module parses local query-template/XML configuration, not Solr HTTP input, and is outside the Solr advisory.
SimplePostTool is a standalone command-line utility that parses a file the user explicitly chose to post; there is no untrusted remote input.

masking: T3 stays reachable after T1/T2 are fixed: the tr branch parses the same request body through a TrAX-created parser before the hardened StAX factory is used, so the residual route becomes visible only once the factories are hardened.

conflicts.what: Hardening the stylesheet factory with FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING or an empty ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET also blocks the legitimate xsl:include that OutputWriterTest exercises (dummy-using-include.xsl:30, OutputWriterTest.java:89-90); the fix must keep solrres: includes resolving.

Refusing transforms or the tr parameter to block the TrAX parse breaks the documented XSLT update path (XsltUpdateRequestHandlerTest.java:68); only the source parser may be hardened, not the transform itself.

A deny-all resolver in SystemIdResolver would also block the XInclude includes the config parser must keep resolving (schema-xinclude.xml:21,24 and solrconfig-xinclude.xml:23-31, asserted by TestXIncludeConfig.java:55); only non-solrres external entities may be refused.

fairness_risks: An XML update or analysis body that legally carries a DOCTYPE (for example an internal DTD used for entity reuse) is refused by the natural disallow-doctype fix.

solrres:-based XInclude in solrconfig/schema must keep working (schema-xinclude.xml:21,24; solrconfig-xinclude.xml:23-31; TestXIncludeConfig.java:55), as must absolute file:// XInclude hrefs that administrators may use.
XSLT update via tr= and the xslt response writer with xsl:include must keep working (XsltUpdateRequestHandlerTest.java:68; OutputWriterTest.java:80-90).
DocumentAnalysisRequestHandler must keep accepting ordinary XML with an encoding declaration (DocumentAnalysisRequestHandlerTest.java:70-77 and 140-147).
The update handler must keep accepting XML with an XML declaration and no DOCTYPE, which is the normal client shape; a fix that refuses all declarations would break every client.

design.why: T1 and T2 are the two independent StAX factories on the server's HTTP XML surface (the likely sites of the published fix and its incomplete sibling), and they require two separate judgements: configure the update loader factory, then find the second, separate handler. T3 is the same request body parsed again by the TrAX transformer whenever tr= is present, so the natural StAX-factory fix leaves it open; it is the deepseek-style absent-protection-with-a-reason-to-dismiss and also the mimo-style how-type fix (a secure XMLReader/secure processing on the transform source rather than on the factory). T4 is the stylesheet-compilation side of the same XSLT subsystem, with a different dismissal (administrator-supplied stylesheets) and a real must-keep-working tension with xsl:include. The four span easy to hard and cover both model profiles; the remaining traps (T5-T12) are client-side, config-file or local-template parsers that the advisory does not cover and that a hidden behavioural test is unlikely to exercise.
